extension.description: Mirror a connected Android device into a sidebar panel and drive it with the mouse.
view.screen.name: Screen
command.launch.title: Launch App
command.reconnect.title: Re-detect Device
capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces: The extension runs the `adb` executable named by `androidPanel.adbPath`, which a workspace could point at an arbitrary program.
capabilities.virtualWorkspaces: The extension needs `adb` and the `scrcpy-server` file on a local disk.
config.mode:
`stream`: create a virtual display through the scrcpy server and receive it as H.264. The device's own screen stays free.

`screencap`: poll the device's own screen. Works without scrcpy, but occupies the device.
config.mode.stream: Decode the scrcpy H.264 stream. Needs the `scrcpy-server` file and an editor whose Chromium provides WebCodecs.
config.mode.screencap: Poll `adb exec-out screencap`. Needs nothing but `adb`, and can only read physical displays.
config.adbPath: Path to the `adb` executable. Leave empty to look on `PATH`, in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\scrcpy`, in the Android SDK's `platform-tools`, and in the usual Unix locations.
config.package:
Package to launch when the panel opens. Leave empty to show whatever is already on the display.

A component (`package/activity`) is started as given, which is how a home app is launched: home apps register no launcher entry, so nothing can be resolved from their package alone. Putting the device's launcher here fills a virtual display with the real home screen and every app on it.
config.intervalMs: `screencap` mode: how often to re-read the screen, in milliseconds. Lower is smoother but costs more.
config.serial: Serial of the device to use. Leave empty to pick automatically, preferring physical devices over emulators.
config.scrcpyServerPath: `stream` mode: path to the `scrcpy-server` file, which ships inside a scrcpy release. Leave empty to search the same places as `adb`.
config.scrcpyVersion: Version of the `scrcpy-server` file. Leave empty to ask the `scrcpy` binary sitting next to it. A value that does not match the server file is refused by the server.
config.newDisplay:
`stream` mode: virtual display to create, e.g. `1440x3120/560`. Leave empty to mirror the device's own screen.

Match the device's real density or the right edge of the screen may be cut off (check with `adb shell wm density`).
config.maxFps: `stream` mode: cap on frames per second. 0 does not cap.
config.keepStreamWhenHidden: `stream` mode: keep the stream running while the panel is hidden. Turning this off destroys the virtual display, which kills the app with it, so reopening the panel starts the app from scratch.
config.maxSize: `stream` mode: cap on the long edge of the encoded frame, in pixels. The device scales the screen down before encoding, which cuts bandwidth and decoding cost sharply. Anything wider than the sidebar looks the same. 0 does not scale.
config.wakeDevice: Wake the device when the panel starts, and in `stream` mode again if a screen timeout puts it back to sleep. A sleeping device swallows injected taps instead of delivering them to the app, so the panel streams fine while nothing responds to a click. This does not unlock the device -- awake and locked is enough -- but the device's own screen does light up.
config.stayAwake: `stream` mode: keep the device awake while it charges (`stay_on_while_plugged_in`). Only needed where a screen timeout puts the device to sleep. This changes a global device setting, so it is off by default.
